message.content:
Here are some practical tips to keep your piano in top shape: | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |-----|----------------|--------------| | **Control humidity** | Pianos are sensitive to moisture; too dry or too wet can warp wood and affect tuning. | • Use a hygrometer inside the piano case.
• Keep humidity between 45‑55 % (ideal for most pianos).
• In dry climates, use a humidifier; in damp areas, use a dehumidifier. | | **Keep it clean** | Dust and grime can dull keys and interfere with action. | • Wipe keys with a soft, dry cloth after each use.
• For deeper cleaning, use a piano‑specific cleaner or a mild soap solution on a damp cloth (never soak). | | **Avoid direct sunlight** | UV rays fade finish and can cause uneven drying. | • Position the piano away from windows or use curtains/UV‑blocking film. | | **Prevent temperature swings** | Rapid changes can expand/contract wood, leading to cracks or tuning instability. | • Keep the room at a steady 20–22 °C (68–72 °F).
• Avoid placing the piano near radiators or vents. | | **Use a piano cover** | Protects from dust, pets, and accidental spills. | • Store a fitted cover when the piano isn’t in use. | | **Check the lid** | A lid that doesn’t close properly can let in drafts. | • Inspect hinges and springs; replace if loose. | | **Regular tuning** | Even a well‑maintained piano will drift over time. | • Schedule a professional tuning every 3–6 months (more often in extreme climates). | | **Inspect the action** | Keys that feel sticky or uneven indicate worn parts. | • Have a technician check hammers, escapement, and dampers annually. | | **Avoid heavy objects** | Dropping items can damage internal components. | • Keep the piano clear of furniture, pets, and clutter. | | **Professional servicing** | Comprehensive checks catch issues before they become costly. | • Arrange a full service (tuning, voicing, regulation) once a year. | **Quick checklist for daily care** 1. **Close the lid** after playing. 2. **Wipe down** the keys and surface. 3. **Check the hygrometer**; adjust humidity if needed. 4. **Make a note** of any unusual sounds or key behavior. By following these habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s sound quality, extend its lifespan, and reduce the need for major repairs. Happy playing!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want tips. We can provide general maintenance tips: humidity control, tuning, cleaning, etc. No function call needed.
